mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain depressed, discretionary trips are displaced toward homebound routines and retail visits stay weak. If this pattern persists for four weeks, RETAIL_REC will remain below its prior four-week mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL remains above 18 and TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below their snapshot levels for most of the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A further week-on-week drop in TRANSIT below its current depressed level signals fewer out-of-home trips and fewer incidental retail stops. Within two weeks this should push RETAIL_REC lower than its recent four-week average.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 2 points week-on-week from its current level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 14 days after TRANSIT posts another week-on-week drop of more than 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM stays near zero or positive while RETAIL_REC remains negative, households are preserving essential shopping but not expanding discretionary shopping. That substitution keeps retail-and-recreation mobility below its prior four-week mean over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC turns positive relative to its last four-week average while GROCERY_PHARM remains at or above 0 for most of the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility from its current depressed level acts as an early reopening signal that spills over into discretionary shopping trips. If PARKS rises by at least 5 points within one week and stays elevated, RETAIL_REC should increase over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises at least 5 points week-on-week from its current level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week mean even though PARKS jumps by at least 5 points and stays above its current level for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both trend upward together, commuting and errand chaining increase, which lifts retail footfall with a short lag. Over the next two weeks, RETAIL_REC should move up relative to the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days after both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT post simultaneous week-on-week increases.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL begins falling from its current high while WORKPLACES begins rising, it indicates easing home confinement and more daytime circulation. This regime shift should translate into higher RETAIL_REC over the next month.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 18 and WORKPLACES rises above -15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below its last-28-day mean for the full 4 weeks after RESIDENTIAL drops below 18 and WORKPLACES rises above -15.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PARKS combined with stable GROCERY_PHARM suggests weather- or calendar-driven outdoor activity rather than broad economic reopening. In that case, discretionary retail mobility will remain soft over the next week even if essentials hold steady.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 4 points while GROCERY_PHARM changes by less than 1 point
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 7 days despite PARKS increasing by at least 4 points and GROCERY_PHARM staying within 1 point of its current level.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT remains deeply negative and WORKPLACES remains below zero, the commuting network stays constrained and consumers consolidate trips near home. That pattern suppresses retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks relative to the previous four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its previous 28-day mean while TRANSIT stays below -25 and WORKPLACES stays below -15 for most of the next 4 weeks.
